::: {.ter-project-brief}
## Design brief

Design a visually organized holder for a related group of tools. It must mount vertically, be removable quickly as one module, and remain useful or stable when taken to a workbench.
:::

## Two operating states

<div class="ter-two-state">
  <div><strong>On the wall</strong><br>Visible · organized · secure · accessible</div>
  <div><strong>On the bench</strong><br>Stable · portable · usable · easy to return</div>
</div>

## System decisions

Consider a French cleat or other approved removable mounting interface, a thicker structural backer, 1/4 inch precision faces, dowels, pins, screws, holes, slots, combs, trays, labels, and shadow-board cues. Design a handle or safe grip only if it does not interfere with mounted use or tool retention.

The wall rail, wall attachment, load path, and structural fasteners must be selected and approved for the actual installation. A thin laser-cut plywood face is not a rated wall-mounting system.

## Test plan

- Load and remove each tool while the module is mounted.
- Remove and carry the complete module using the intended grip.
- Place it on the bench and use tools without holding the module.
- Check tipping, sliding, sharp edges, snagged cords, and tool collisions.
- Confirm the module returns to the wall without a delicate alignment routine.
- Revise at least one dimension or feature from test evidence.

[Explore French-cleat modules](../../teaching-materials/laser-cutting/?type=french-cleat#library) and [tool-holder kits](../../teaching-materials/laser-cutting/?type=tool-holders#library) as component references.
